# fastf 3.6.0 — the pane reads the file

A note with a second line lost it. `fastf note add ID0047 -` took the whole of
stdin, the editor took whatever you saved, the app's quick note took Alt-Enter
for a new line — and every one of them wrote the first line as a note and left
the rest in the file where nothing would ever read it back. The pane beside
the list trusted what it had read until a verb inside the app told it
otherwise, so a line you added in your editor never showed. Notes and the
journal were two sections that meant the same thing. The mouse ate your text
selection. And what moved on the screen moved like a glitch.

This release is about the file, and about looking at it.

## Notes are the journal

One section, `## Notes`, holding dated entries — and a note keeps every line
it has:

```markdown
## Notes

- 2026-04-20T14:32:11Z — finished final mix
- 2026-04-22T09:10:03Z — client made a poem for me
  oh you who edit my videos
  road is long
```

The lines after the first are indented, so nothing inside a note can start
another one or end the section. A note written on one line is written exactly
as before, so a diff over an old file shows only the line that was added.

**The reader is lenient.** Type a note by hand and it counts: a line at the
left margin starting with `- ` and a date, with or without the `—`, starts a
note, and every line until the next one belongs to it — which means the files
the old writer broke read correctly now, second lines and all. Text above the
first entry is one undated note. `## notes:` is a heading; `###` is not.

**Older projects keep their `## Journal`.** Nothing moves: new notes go under
it, and the pane and `fastf notes` read it as they always did.

`fastf notes` prints every line of a note, and `--since` now refuses a date
fastf never wrote — `2026-6-1` sorted after every note of the year and hid
them all, the way `recent --since` already refused to.

## Todos

```markdown
## Todo

- [x] ingested the footage
- [ ] deliver the video
```

The pane lists them under their own rule; Enter ticks one, or unticks it,
by rewriting the one character inside the brackets. An add row appends one.
The command line does not have a todo verb yet; the file is yours to edit,
and the pane follows.

## The pane reads the file

A note is its own rows now — the day it was written, its first line, every
further line under it — the latest five, with `… n earlier` opening them all.
Enter on a note edits it in place: Enter for a new line, Ctrl-S to save,
emptied and saved to remove it. Enter on a todo toggles it. Every section that
can grow ends in a row that adds to it — **add a tag**, **add a note**, **add
a todo** — and the hint bar's Enter says what it will do to the row under the
cursor.

**And it keeps reading.** What the pane shows is `PROJECT_INFO.md` as it is on
disk. Edit the file in another window and the pane follows within a second,
with no key pressed; F5 asks at once. A note or todo that changed on disk since
the pane read it is refused rather than overwritten. A row whose tags disagree
with the file takes the file's.

## The mouse is a setting, and off

Text selects as in any program again. The app no longer asks the terminal to
report the mouse unless you tell it to, and the wheel still scrolls the list —
every modern terminal turns it into arrow keys on the alternate screen.
`fastf config set mouse on`, the Mouse row of the settings, or *Mouse capture
on or off* in the command palette bring back a click on a row and a wheel that
moves three; hold Shift to select text then.

## Motion that guides the eye

Motion here has one job: to take the eye to the one thing that just changed,
and then to let go. It used to flash — a wash held for half a second and gone,
which is what a terminal looks like when it is broken.

- **A row a verb just changed lights up and fades.** So does a pane row an edit
  went into, a note just added, a todo just ticked.
- **The focus eases between the panes.** Border and title move from their
  resting colour to their focused one, and the pane you left goes the other
  way at the same moment.
- **The row you were on pulses after a sort or a filter.** The selection is
  kept, so it is somewhere else on the screen now; the pulse says where.
- **A message arrives under a wash** on the status line, and still dims on its
  way out.

In truecolor the fades are real, toward the dark the palette is drawn on. In
the sixteen ANSI colours there is no ramp, so a wash is held and let go and the
focus lands at once. `fastf config set motion off` is still every frame a hard
cut, and a palette with no colour still never moves.

## Nothing else changed

No template format, no config file format. One new setting, `mouse`. Every
`PROJECT_INFO.md` written before this still parses and is never rewritten
unasked; `fastf note add` takes the same three inputs. One behaviour change on
the command line: `fastf notes --since` with a value that is not a date exits
1 instead of quietly listing nothing.

Full key list: [docs/cli.md](https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/blob/main/docs/cli.md#keys)
